turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, Mrs Pillay. I did your vitals quickly. Blood pressure is 132 over 84, pulse is 76, and your temperature is 36.8. On the script it says amlodipine ten milligrams every morning.
[SEG0002] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Ten? Shame, no. I pack her pill box every Sunday. It's the five milligram tablet, one in the morning. I've been doing it for months.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Eish, I don't look at the packet, hey. I just swallow whatever is in the Monday slot. Yoh, that waiting room was hectic, the baby didn't stop screaming.
[SEG0004] person_4 (DOCTOR): Come through, both of you, sit down. I'm Dr Naidoo. What's been happening?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): It's this burning when I pass urine, again. It's the third time this year. Well, actually, maybe the fourth, I lose track. Um...
[SEG0006] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, the burning has been nearly two weeks. She's been holding her stomach, and she's off her food, she hardly touches supper.

[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): No, not two weeks. It started on Saturday, so about five days. And I'm eating fine, really, I had a whole plate of bobotie last night, it was lekker. I just get tired in the afternoons, that's all.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Alright, so burning when you wee, five days by your count, longer by hers. That sounds sore. Any blood in the urine, or pain up in your back, by the kidneys?

[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): No blood. My back is fine, it's not that. It burns when I go, and I'm running to the loo all the time, even at night. I nearly didn't make it at the robot on Main Road this morning, can you believe it.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): Have you felt feverish, or shivery?

[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): No fever. I checked at home, the thermometer was normal. I bought it at the pharmacy in Cavendish, and the queue was out the door with this flu going around, people coughing everywhere...
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Mm. And down below, any vaginal discharge, or itching?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. It's just the urine, I'm sure. I'd rather not go into all of that, it's embarrassing.
[SEG0014] person_2 (CAREGIVER): She told me yesterday there was an itch, when she was getting dressed. She was quite bothered.
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Well, actually... ja. There is a bit of an itch, and maybe a little whitish discharge. I was embarrassed. It's not bad.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Thank you, that is useful, and there's no need to be shy here. Have you taken anything for the burning?

[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): I took my sister's leftover antibiotic. Cipro, five hundred milligrams, by mouth, one in the morning and one at night. I did that for two days, then I stopped because my tummy went funny, loose stool. That settled once I stopped, and I know I shouldn't have.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): When did you stop?

[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Yesterday. So only two days. My sister from Durban left the box after she visited, she had a sinus thing. We did a braai that Saturday, and the dog stole a sausage right off the table, little menace.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Okay. And you're still taking the amlodipine every morning, by mouth, for your blood pressure?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja, every morning, by mouth. I've had the high blood pressure for years, it's ongoing. I don't miss doses because she packs them.
[SEG0022] person_2 (CAREGIVER): And it is the five milligram one. The bottle in the cupboard says 5 mg. I don't know where ten comes from.
[SEG0023] person_1 (NURSE): I'm only reading the electronic script, doctor. It says ten milligrams. I can print the screen if it helps.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): We won't guess the dose in this room. We'll straighten the script out separately. Any other medicines, or any allergies?

[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): No allergies that I know of. Sometimes I take a Panado for a headache, but I haven't needed one in ages. Oh, and I drink rooibos all day, does that count? Thandi makes it strong.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Rooibos is fine. Let me feel your tummy, if you're comfortable. Just lie back.
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): My feet are freezing, I should have worn socks. The wind on the way in was mad.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): Abdomen is soft. There's a bit of tenderness just above the pubic bone. No tenderness when I tap over either kidney.
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja, that low spot is sore when you press. The rest is okay.

[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): I think this is most likely another bladder infection. With the itch and the discharge I also can't rule out a bit of thrush alongside. I'd rather not give more antibiotic until the urine result is back.
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): So no more of my sister's pills. Sharp. I was worried I'd made a mess of it.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Please don't take any more of those. Drink plenty of water today and the next few days. We'll send a midstream urine to the lab, and do a dipstick here.
[SEG0033] person_1 (NURSE): I can collect the sample and do the dipstick now, and I'll send the culture if you sign it.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, please. Dipstick now, and microscopy and culture to the lab. That's booked.
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): Do I come back, or do you phone me?
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Come back if it's not settling in three days. Sooner if you get a fever or pain in your side. We'll phone as well if the culture says you need a particular antibiotic.
[SEG0037] person_2 (CAREGIVER): I'll bring her if she gets worse. She stays alone in the flat. I come on weekday mornings.
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja, second floor in Observatory. I'm not helpless, I just like the company. And the rooibos.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good. So, lots of water, no more leftover cipro, urine off today, and see me again if you're not better in three days. Anything else worrying you?
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): No, I think that's the lot. Thanks, hey. I just hope the parking meter has enough coins, those things swallow money.
[SEG0041] person_1 (NURSE): I'll walk you to the toilet for the sample when you're done. Midstream, I'll explain it there.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Perfect. Take care, Mrs Pillay.
[SEG0043] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Pleasure, doctor. I'll wait with her.
[SEG0044] person_3 (PATIENT): Come, before that meter expires. Cheers.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

omissions.text: Amlodipine dose is disputed: nurse/electronic script says 10 mg every morning, while caregiver states patient has been taking 5 mg every morning for months from the bottle/pill box; current medication record lacks the disputed dose details.
Negative finding asked and answered: no vaginal discharge or itching was initially denied by the patient before she later revised this history.
Negative finding asked and answered: patient denied feeling shivery.
Symptom detail: urinary urgency was described, including nearly not making it to the toilet this morning.
Plan detail: specifically avoid giving more antibiotic until the urine result is back.
